accuracy.evidence: Checked against NC KS1 working scientifically (observing closely, using simple equipment; identifying and classifying). Hand lens described as a convex magnifier giving an enlarged view of detail already present, sharp only at the right object distance, typically 2-10x; the lab uses 4x. Sun warning matches standard school safety advice: never view the Sun through any lens, and a lens in sunlight can ignite material.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented KS1 slips: the lens makes the object itself bigger (step 1 prediction 'a bigger, heavier leaf', challenge tag grow), pressing the lens on the object or giving up when blurry (tag press), opinion words like nice or good instead of observable properties (tag opinion), calling two things the same after a glance (tag same), using a lens for every question and confusing how long (length) with how long (time) (tag tool), and looking at the Sun (tag sun).

lab_distinct.evidence: flaghlens is built on a draggable magnifier that redraws the same scene 4x inside a clipped circle, with a focus distance that blurs the view, so the details exist at 1x and are revealed, not invented. flaglook is a drawing-from-life lab, flagsense matches senses and flagobsvs sorts facts from guesses; lab_distinct gate under 30% against every other flagship.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers that the veins, edge hairs and aphid were on the leaf before the lens arrived, finds the sharp distance by moving the slider (too close and too far both blur), sees leaf 1 and leaf 2 differ only after viewing both edges, and gets a tool-specific reason when a question card lands on the wrong tool; the step text confirms each idea afterwards.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 'nothing new' or 'a bigger, heavier leaf' before the hunt, 'press the lens flat on the leaf' before focusing, 'it is nice' for the shell, 'yes, same colour, same leaf' before the close comparison, and 'a hand lens' for measuring a worm's length.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge questions with shuffled answers; every wrong answer carries a tag (grow, press, opinion, tool, same, sun) whose message names that slip, e.g. 'That word says what you think. Use a looking word: colour, shape, size, texture or pattern.'

readability.evidence: Kid text is in short sentences with everyday words (lens, bigger, blurry, sharp, bumpy, stripy) and passes the family kid readability target in validate_lessons; adult text names the curriculum strand, the optics in plain terms and six common mistakes. Canvas labels are one to five words.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate is clean. Each kid paragraph adds one idea (what a lens does, details already there, focusing, looking words, comparing, choosing tools and safety) and each lab step practises exactly one of them; no repeated template text.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark: the tall 1.15 canvas keeps the leaf about 280 px wide and the lens radius about 78 px, word chips are about 110 x 50 px, the tool boxes and safety panels are large tap targets, and the young-mode buttons are 56 px; nothing is clipped at 390 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin (The middle / The edge / Near the stalk, Closer / Farther, one button per word, Look at leaf 1 or 2 then the three answers, Pick then a tool, the two safety choices); the canvas aria-label is updated with every spoken result; walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone.

sources: Department for Education, National Curriculum in England: science programmes of study, Key Stage 1 working scientifically: observing closely, using simple equipment; identifying and classifying; using observations to suggest answers to questions
CLEAPSS / ASE Be Safe! guidance: never look directly at the Sun, with or without optical aids such as hand lenses
Hand lens (simple magnifier) optics: a convex lens gives an enlarged, upright virtual image when the object is inside its focal length; typical hand lenses magnify about 2x to 10x
